carry_forward.detail: A setup and its token trace replay exactly from (run, game, side) at any batch shape, because each draw is an inverse-CDF lookup keyed by its own seed. The recorded float32 behavior probabilities are bitwise identical only at the SAME batch shape: a batched GEMM is not shape-invariant. Measured delta at 200 vs 1: <= 1e-6. No training consequence -- the ratio denominator is always the recorded probability -- but a verifier that re-derives a setup at a different pool size must expect it.
carry_forward.title: Cross-batch-shape replay is exact in tokens, not in recorded floats

carry_forward.detail: -min(r*delta, clip(r)*delta) is asymmetric in the sign of delta. On-policy (r = 1) a reward flip negates the policy gradient exactly. Off-policy it changes which rows are gradient-active instead: measured at a 0.2 clip on a deliberately far-off-policy model, 72.5% of rows clipped and the flipped gradient had cosine +0.46 with the original. Anyone re-running the flip test must isolate it as the gate does.
carry_forward.title: The reward-flip property holds on the surrogate, not on the clipped loss

carry_forward.detail: The conditional-entropy head starts near zero and must predict I/10, which is about 2.7 on the initial masked model, so L_h starts around 12 while L_pi is order 0.3. The pre-clip gradient norm is therefore far above the 0.5 clip for the first iterations and effectively every early step is clipped. Not a defect -- it is the head converging -- but Agent 4's telemetry should expect it rather than read it as instability.
carry_forward.title: L_h dominates the setup loss at hour 0

superseded_finding.mechanism: The setup advantage's entropy term is alpha*(I/10 - h), and L_h explicitly trains h toward I/10. The term is therefore the residual of a prediction that another loss term is actively making accurate, so it converges to zero by construction rather than by accident. Measured: the conditional-entropy head converges within roughly ten iterations (L_h 3.33 -> 0.10), the residual |I/10 - h| collapses from 2.81 to about 0.28 and then stays flat for the rest of the run, and the entropy term goes from being commensurate with the outcome term at iteration 1 (1.2x) to roughly 100x weaker for the remaining 98% of the run.
superseded_finding.not_established: This agent did NOT test the alternative form. That the normalized term provides no sustained pressure is measured; that an uncentered term would hold entropy up without destabilising training is NOT, and would need its own soak.
superseded_finding.severity: blocks the gate; requires an operator decision before launch
superseded_finding.soak_caveat: The soak's move policy is a uniform-random legal fixture and 83% of its games were draws, so the magnitude of the entropy decline is not a production forecast. The structural point -- that the entropy term self-cancels once its baseline is learned -- is independent of the outcome distribution and does carry over.
superseded_finding.the_papers_asymmetry_may_be_load_bearing: The paper regresses h to H/10 while its delta uses (H - h). Agent 1 read the mismatch as a units error and normalized both sides (D4). But that asymmetry is exactly what makes the paper's bonus UNCENTERED: (H - h) ~ (H - H/10) = 0.9*H, which scales with entropy instead of vanishing. Under D4's consistent-units reading the term is centered and regularizes nothing. Agent 1's objection to the literal form -- that 0.9*alpha*H is about 5.6 at alpha=0.1 against an outcome term bounded by 2 -- is correct in RAW NATS. Expressed in the normalized I/10 units the same uncentered form is 0.9*alpha*(I/10), about 0.56 at alpha=0.1, which is commensurate with the outcome term. A form satisfying both of D4's stated constraints therefore exists and was not considered when D4 was resolved.
superseded_finding.title: The D4-normalized entropy term is a centered residual and provides no sustained entropy pressure
superseded_finding.why_the_alpha_anneal_is_not_the_cause: D3's compressed anneal was the recorded risk, and it is real but second-order here. The entropy term was already about 25x subordinate to the outcome term at iteration 10, when alpha was still 0.032 -- a third of its starting value and eight times its floor. The residual collapse, not the anneal, is what removed the pressure.

what_agent_3_did_not_establish: setup STRENGTH. The soak's move policy is a uniform-random legal fixture, so a better setup distribution has nothing to be better against. The soak establishes legality, diversity and a working outcome-to-update path, and nothing more.
